observations: Photo 0: Back of a gold-colored iPhone with a large camera module containing three lenses, a flash, and a microphone. The Apple logo is visible. The phone appears to have a protective case or skin covering the back.

Photo 1: Same phone from a slightly different angle, held in hand, showing the same back design and case. The lighting reflects off the surface, suggesting a smooth, possibly plastic or silicone cover.

Photo 2: Screen showing the 'About' section of iOS settings. Capacity is listed as 512 GB, available space is 483.22 GB. Network Provider Lock shows 'No SIM restrictions'. EID is visible. The top status bar shows time 08:03, Wi-Fi, and battery icon. The notch is present, consistent with iPhone 12 or later models.
No photo shows the front screen, the model name, or the serial number. No photo shows the box or accessories.

claims.evidence: No photo shows the model name. The camera module and notch design are inconsistent with iPhone 17 Pro Max (which does not exist as of 2024). The design matches iPhone 12/13/14/15 Pro Max. The 'About' screen does not show the model name.
Photo 2 shows 'Network Provider Lock: No SIM restrictions'.
No photo shows battery health percentage. The battery icon in photo 2 is not detailed enough to assess health.
Photos show the back with a case/skin, but no close-up of screen, edges, or buttons. Scratches or wear are not visible.

risks.risk: The phone is not an iPhone 17 Pro Max (non-existent model) but likely an older model (e.g., iPhone 12/13/14/15 Pro Max), which affects value.
risks.proof: Photo showing the model name on the back or in settings, or a clear shot of the front with the model name.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as an older model, not as a non-existent iPhone 17 Pro Max.

risks.risk: Battery health is not shown and may be poor, affecting usability and resale value.
risks.proof: Photo of the 'Battery Health' section in settings showing percentage and peak performance capability.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if battery is degraded (e.g., below 80%).

risks.risk: The phone may be a refurbished or non-genuine unit, or have hidden damage (screen, buttons, charging port).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the front screen, edges, buttons, charging port, and speaker grills.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially damaged or non-genuine.

risks.risk: The phone may be iCloud locked or have other software restrictions not visible in the 'About' screen.
risks.proof: Video or photo showing the phone being turned on, logged into a different Apple ID, or showing the 'Activation Lock' screen.

proof_requests: Photo of the front screen showing the model name (e.g., 'iPhone 14 Pro Max') or the model number in settings.
Photo of the 'Battery Health' section in settings.
Close-up photos of the front screen, edges, buttons, and charging port.
Video showing the phone being turned on and logged into a different Apple ID, or showing the 'Activation Lock' screen.
response.reason: The seller claims an iPhone 17 Pro Max, which does not exist, and the model cannot be confirmed from the photos. Battery health and physical condition are unverified. The item cannot be priced accurately without proof of the actual model, battery health, and physical condition.
